replay.right: Adaptive Uncertainty-Guided Experience Replay for Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Learning. Neural networks that learn a sequence of tasks suffer from catastrophic forgetting. Replay-based methods reduce it by storing past samples, but most fill and sample the memory uniformly, so a fixed budget is spent on redundant, easily classified examples. This paper proposes Adaptive Uncertainty-Guided Experience Replay (AUER), in which the model’s own predictive uncertainty decides which samples are prioritised for replay. Each sample is scored by fusing Monte Carlo Dropout variance, predictive entropy and mutual information. The fused score is combined with a diversity term to give a replay priority, which is converted into sampling probabilities with a softmax. Replay uses a fixed-capacity buffer of 2000 samples and a fixed replay ratio, so the network, optimiser and memory budget match those of standard experience replay. .
